For every commutative ring $R$, the coefficientwise addition and convolution multiplication of [[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]] make $R[x]$ a commutative ring.
For $S\subseteq R$, define $(S)$ to be the intersection of all two-sided ideals of $R$ containing $S$.
The quotient ring $R/I$ with $(r+I)(s+I)=rs+I$.
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $g\in R[x]$ be monic. For every $f\in R[x]$ there are unique $q,r\in R[x]$ such that $$ f=qg+r,\qquad r=0\ \text{or}\ \deg r<\deg g. $$

derivations.claim: Let Q=R[X]/(G). By [F2] and [F3], this is a quotient ring. Since G is monic of degree two, [F4] gives every class in Q a representative a(p)+b(p)X of degree at most one in X. If two such representatives define the same class, their difference is a multiple of G and has degree less than two; uniqueness in [F4] forces the difference to be zero. Thus this representative is unique.

In Q, the relation X^2-pX-1=0 gives X(X-p)=1, so X is invertible with inverse X-p. The homomorphism Q→Z[x,x^{-1}] sending p↦x-x^{-1} and X↦x respects G=0. Conversely, sending x↦X defines a homomorphism Z[x,x^{-1}]→Q because X^{-1}=X-p. The composites fix the generators p,X and x, respectively, so these homomorphisms are inverse. The unique representatives from step 1.1 therefore give the asserted unique Laurent decomposition.

derivations.claim: For a state with k B-smoothings, [F2] gives a stack of k copies of e1 and 3-k copies of I. If k=0, the closure has two circles by [F3]. If k≥1, repeated use of e1^2=δe1 from [F4] and the one-circle closure of e1 in [F3] gives exactly k circles. There are binomial(3,k) choices, so [F1] gives the complete grouped state sum with rows (0,1,2,A^3δ), (1,3,1,3A), (2,3,2,3A^{-1}δ), (3,1,3,A^{-3}δ^2).

Substituting δ=-A^2-A^{-2} into the grouped sum gives <T>=A^3δ+3A+3A^{-1}δ+A^{-3}δ^2=A^{-7}-A^{-3}-A^5. By [F5] the closure is one knot component, and [F6] gives writhe 3. Thus f_T(A)=(-A^3)^{-3}<T>=A^{-4}+A^{-12}-A^{-16}; under [A1], [F7] identifies this with V_T(t)=t+t^3-t^4.

Write x^n=A_n(p)+B_n(p)x. From x^2=px+1, multiplication by x gives A_{n+1}=B_n and B_{n+1}=A_n+pB_n. Starting with x^0=1 and x^1=x yields the complete recurrence table through n=8 displayed in the item, including x^2, x^6, and x^8.
Combining the rows for n=2,6,8 gives a(p)=1-3p^2-4p^4-p^6 and b(p)=-6p^3-5p^5-p^7. Uniqueness in [F9] therefore gives f_2(T)=(-3,0)^T≠0.

The computed Jones polynomial is not 1. Under [A1], [F8] gives V_U=1 and invariance under ambient isotopy, so T is nontrivial. The displayed braid has three crossings, so under [A2] and [F10] its crossing-number set contains 3 and c(T)≤3.
